scope: O2 step 1 expansion, Stage A only. Indexed Binance notices are discovery hints.
method: Search date-partitioned listing, settlement/delisting and contract-change queries. Narrow intervals and target specific unresolved examples on a second pass.
Keep exact indexed announcement or blog URLs. Select an English variant actually seen in the index and record observed variants. Group duplicates by notice ID.
Use the publication date shown in the indexed response. Do not infer publication from the effective date in the title. Unresolved publication results are held by query for rechecking.
Discard known post-cutoff publications and updates before symbol extraction. Record only counts for discarded or ambiguously dated hits.

Recognize contract symbols and dates in the notice heading, launch table or applicable futures clauses returned by the index. For older notices, a base with explicitly stated USDT margin can supply an inferred symbol spelling. Resolve mixed-date statements by symbol. Review contract changes, postponements and symbol reuse separately.
Exclude spot, delivery, COIN-M and non-USDT evidence. A spot rebrand alone cannot establish a futures transition.
limitations: Date filters and domain filters do not constrain all provider results. Some queries returned out-of-request-window notices that were within the global cutoff. Listed query counts count hit occurrences, including duplicates across queries.
An initial parsing attempt did not retain individual results. Its exact queries, status and available counts remain in the log. Replacement and targeted queries supplied the retained evidence.

The index returned finite ranked results and some queries errored. Pre-2023 openings and intervening contract changes remain incomplete. The response does not establish exchange-wide completeness or point-in-time universe membership.
